utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I'd like to welcome all those present. I am sorry for this 10-minute lateness this morning. We had some technical problems. Luckily, the problem was solved in time. Mr. Registrar, it would be a good idea if somebody from the Registry was here half an hour before the sitting begins to see that everything is in order, to see if the clock's working, that the lights are all switched on, and everything else is ready for the start of work in the best possible conditions. I hope that our witness has arrived, is here. I'm going to ask the usher to bring him in very quickly. Yes, Mr. Coric. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I'd like to remind you once again of the problem of my Defence team, whether my request reached the Trial Chamber and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as your request was concerned for the time, yes, we have taken that on board, and it is up to your Defence counsel of one of the two proposals. Now, in that respect, I don't have any other information, but I would like -- I'm going to ask to be informed. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my information comes directly from the Registrar. They expect a response from you, and that's what they've been telling me for the past 10 days. They've been telling me that, and they've been telling me the counsel that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we're going to take the matter up with the Registrar, but it does come under the competencies of the Registrar, under Articles 44 and 45, to see about the two individuals that you have proposed and then see if they conform with the conditions. So that is a job that the Registrar does, not I myself. I can't appoint a counsel for you and say, yes, such-and-such a person is fine. But don't worry, I'll inform myself of the matter, and we will inform you in due course very quickly. Now, Madam Usher, would you have the witness brought in, please. Yes, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with respect to the Bruno Stojic Defence, we still have technical problems with the LiveNote. We can continue, but perhaps the registrar could help us during the break. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You may be seated. We're glad to see you back, sir. As you know, you've come to continue your testimony and the cross-examination. Of course if everything goes well, as I said yesterday, your examination will last for five hours and a quarter, and as we have six hours sitting today, in principle at the end of the day you will be able to leave and go back home. Having said that, I'm going to give the floor to the Defence. I don't know who is going to start off. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mufti.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to say something? I have a remark to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During my last examination, Mr. Kovacic said something, made a statement that has no foundation, is not based on justice and the truth and might have an effect in people drawing the wrong conclusions, and this is what it's about: There's a fragment upon which the gentleman built up his defence, and that was linked to the extremist behaviour in very extreme situations when it came to prisoners, and he said that that was a model of behaviour and that people had the duty to behave that way according to Islamic law. Now, I found this little booklet when I was home, and I found that this was a trick, and I'm going to give you those quotations, if you like. You will, of course, decide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll look at the problem, but perhaps some of the other counsel will raise the problem again and this will give you an opportunity to say what you wish to say. There we have it. Anyway, thank you for intervening. Counsel Karnavas has the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning again. Okay, since you brought up the topic, let's get right to it. In your testimony - and I'm quoting from page 2472, on 24 May, 2006 - you were asked a question by the Prosecutor with respect to your duties as mufti, which as I understand is pretty much at the same level as a bishop in, say, the Catholic or the Orthodox religions. And in that question you said that part your duties were contributing to the affirmation of religious values in the most proper manner. That was what you said. Do you recall saying that, and I take it you stand by that. Now, first and foremost, I want to make sure that we're clear. I am not, and I don't believe Mr. Kovacic did either, or any of my colleagues will say, that you were the author of the "Instructions for Muslim Fighters." As you indicated, that came from Zenica, but you also indicated that that was either authored by or it was published with the approval of the Zenica mufti; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that theirs -- the head of the Islamic church in Bosnia is in Sarajevo. That's Reis-ul-Ulema. I don't know if I'm pronouncing it correctly.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And his closest advisors, associates, his peers, I would assume he's somewhat like first among equals, maybe slightly higher, they're all the muftis in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you being one of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I think that there's no dilemma in us knowing that during the war, unfortunately, there were individuals on all sides that, you know, committed extreme acts that no one should have to tolerate in a civilised society. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And unfortunately again, some foreign fighters came, perhaps on all sides, but since you're here, we're speaking of Islamic fighters that came, and with them they brought traditions, practices, habits which are not necessarily -- or do not necessarily comport with the Geneva Conventions. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On all sides. That was a good thing you said. There were groups of people on all sides. We can call them Mujahedin if you like. But anyway, they existed in the army or, rather, attached to the army or independent units of Mujahedins, and the Croatian Defence had mercenaries, and the Serb side had mercenaries as well. They were legionaries and they did dirty things. And it is my duty to be quite frank and tell you all this. The positions, to a certain extent, of the Mujahedin attached to the army is a little different from the legionaries and mercenaries on the other sides because they joined the aggressive forces, whereas the Mujahedin nonetheless, although what you said some of it is true, they did nevertheless help the victims; the Bosniaks, the Muslims who were the victims of the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. You know being -- I think, aside from being a religious leader, we're also colleagues in the sense that you're a trained lawyer. Maybe in a different kind of law, but nonetheless you're lawyer like I am, and you would agree with me that the Geneva Conventions does not make a distinction between aggressor or non-aggressor, or defender, whatever you want to call the term. All sides to a conflict have to abide by certain rules; right? So it doesn't really make a difference at the end of the day. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in this particular instance, it would appear that a religious leader who was among the family and closest advisors of the Reis-ul-Ulema and one of your own colleagues introduced a booklet that clearly provides for practices that are not -- that are inconsistent not only with the Geneva Conventions but also with the laws as they existed back then in the former Yugoslavia, including Bosnia-Herzegovina, whether it was the Republic, the Socialist Republic, or what have you. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've put things very rightly. However, to present a view of the Koran of universal importance is not -- that is applied, that is to say apply religious rules in -- is differently applied in different environments. So there are some universal positions, but it is quite normal to respect the state legislation in a country and, for example, in -- that Bosnia-Herzegovina is not an Islamic state. And -- with your permission, may I just be allowed to finish. These are instructions. These instructions have to do more with the moral code of conduct. That is the important part. It is a moral code of conduct. So they cannot be applied in Bosnia-Herzegovina, all the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You say that they cannot be applied, but when you look at the instructions they're for Bosnian -- or for fighters within Bosnia-Herzegovina. They talk about the homeland of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it's put out by a -- by a mufti of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it would appear, sir - and you can answer yes or no on this question and then we'll move on - that no one within the hierarchy of the Islamic Community, the Reis-ul-Ulema or any of the other muftis, including you, took a public position and said no, this kind of conduct is inconsistent with our values, our laws, the laws of the international community that we have adopted. No one in -- no one from the Islamic Community, the higher-ups, took that position. And by not taking that position, in essence it was like giving a green light to this sort of behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Again, this has now gone on for about 12 lines of text and is argument rather than questioning, and especially this last part. Not only does Mr. Karnavas state the question, but then he states the answer that he -- his argument that he wants to make. By "giving a green light," Your Honour, that goes beyond putting a question to this witness. It's simply an argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you take a public position, sir? Yes or no. There is no explanation on this one. You either stood in front of your congregation, in front of the folks, or got on the radio and said do not apply at least this piece of instruction which talks about liquidation of prisoners. Did you take a public position? Yes or no. The answer --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, countless times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Publicly.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, please, if we're going to be proper, do you have the original of the text of the instructions, the set of instructions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in fact, I'm going to be introducing it into evidence. I'm just asking you, did you take a public position where you said, Mujahedin, you folks who have come from Iran or from Afghanistan, or from Iraq or wherever you come from, and you homegrown folks, including the Efendi Halilovic, one of your colleagues, do not liquidate prisoners as these instructions published by the mufti of Zenica for fighters within Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you take a public position? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. With that, I accept it, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, the document that I'm referring to is 1D 00505 and I'll be introducing this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Moving on to Naser Efendi Halilovic. I just have a few questions on this. You indicated last time that you were here that this gentleman was from the Konjic area, wanted to go back to assist in -- in protecting his homeland, fighting against the aggressors, and which is why you, along with the other members of the Islamic Community, I guess gave him a leave of absence, for lack of a better term. It was a leave of absence of his religious duties so he could fight.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And there's nothing strange in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would you agree with me on this point: That when he goes there to the field, that he's not looked upon as just another fighter, another Muslim or Bosniak, but he's looked upon by his colleagues or his -- his -- his friends, his compatriots, his fellow fighters, as someone who is a religious leader? You would agree with me on that, wouldn't you? They would look to him; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it seems to me -- now, you indicated that you did not get this letter from -- or the attachment that was sent to you along with the letter, and it was introduced as D -- as 2D 00016 by, I believe, my good colleague from Sarajevo, Ms. Nozica. In this particular document, it clearly states that as early 1990, this gentleman joined -- he took -- he took an active role in SDA politics in the Konjic municipality and was promoting fundamentalism in public appearances. Now, this is 1990. Okay? Let's me ask you this: Back in 1990, nothing was happening in Zepa or Srebrenica as you had indicated that's why he was going to fight. 1990. Let me tell you, I'm familiar with the war, okay? Nothing happens until about 1992, 1993, in the Srebrenica area. And then, of course, we know what happened in 1995. But that's not a dilemma. But here they're talking about him as early as 1990. Here's one of your fellows or your colleagues or somebody underneath you actively engaging in SDA politics and preaching fundamentalism.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just tell me who those allegations are that he's propagating fundamentalism, promoting fundamentalism? The rest is quite true. But I'd like to know who made this assessment about promoting fundamentalism.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It's the head of SIS. Okay?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, well, that's a vital point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to get to that. We're going to get to that at some point because, as I understand it - and maybe I don't want to get too far ahead of myself - but as I understand it, you have some sort of experience first-hand with -- with the security services, because at least there are some documentations that you were working for the security services as early as 1976 and onwards; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But there is documentation. Whether you were working or not, there's documentation. You even have a code name assigned to you in the documentation. I mean, we could go to it right now, if you like.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with your permission, I can address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm asking you is there documentation that refers to you as Rusmir? That's your cross name, your code name, Rusmir, as being one of those individuals that was assisting the security services in the old Yugoslavian days, when that was kind of a common practice the US seems to have adopted these days, spying and so on on its own citizens, but back in those days, according to the documentation - it's been made public as well- you had a code name called Rusmir, and apparently you were providing vital information on your fellow members within the Islamic community including -- including Alija Izetbegovic. I'm not saying whether it's true or not. I'm saying there is documentation. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, why doesn't Mr. Kovacic [sic] put the documents to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to do that -- May I do my cross, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This all came up in the -- Everyone in the courtroom knows about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we've understood the problem. I assume, Mr. Karnavas, that the document is one you're going to present to us. Because you're making an oral assertion, I assume you're backing it up with a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're absolutely certain, Your Honour. I would like the gentleman to first say yea or nay. You know, if the documents are there, I can show them. I don't want to have a big discussion. I'm not -- as to whether he was in fact a double agent, a triple agent, or what have you, but if he first acknowledges that there is documentation, then I can show the documentation to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is public documentation regarding your activities within the security services? Okay. Very well. Let's look at -- since this is taking longer than I would like, let's look at -- yes what? There is documentation? 1D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. There is no answer on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked the question. Shall we wait for the witness's answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. I assumed that the translators had already completed my question and the gentleman who, as I understand also speaks English, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going much too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise to you, sir, as well, and to the translators and interpreters and all the folks in the technical booths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The best thing would be to ask the question again and then we can have the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have seen or you have heard of documentation out there in the public where it makes reference to you being within the security services as early as 1996 [sic] and onwards, and where even in one particular document it refers to you, with a code name, as Rusmir, R-u-s-m-i-r.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if I could just show you the documents. I don't want to have a lengthy discussion, but simply if you could look at the documents. I'll first look and show you document D 0047 -- 427, and I merely want you to -- to look at -- The transcript should be 1976 as opposed to 1996. That was on page 12, line 17, and I want to thank my colleague for pointing that out. But if we could show this document. Okay. And I just want you to look at number 40 on the document and see whether that is your name and whether that is your correct date of birth in one of the columns. Again, it's 1D 00427. If it's not working, I have -- we can put it on the ELMO. Madam Usher, if you could help us out here. This document, by the way, came from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Scott. Let's have a look at the document on the overhead projector before you say what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also, yeah, I have a clean copy in English as well. I don't know if Your Honours have a copy of it, but -- they don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, potentially very serious allegations are being made against this witness, and the document that's been put in front us now, at least what I see -- if I am missing a page, I'll stand to be - and invite to be corrected, in fact, if I'm missing something, but what has been given to me and what I see is a list of names which is something apparently taken out of a document that starts on number 33. I don't know what 1 through 32 is. I don't even know where this document came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, I can help --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There should be some provenance given for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'm surprised and shocked, actually, that the Prosecutor would even say that, because this was an exhibit in a previous case where he, in fact, not only was the Prosecutor but I also understand might have even directed the witness. So if you look at the very first page, it says that it comes from the Naletelic aka Tuta case. This was in the EDS system. That's where we got it from. Or the JDB, I'm sorry. So that's where the document came from. And then I would like to show the gentleman the next document -- incidentally, let's get that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now 40, that is your name, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to accept that, Your Honour. The fact that it came from another case doesn't tell us the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was accepted in the other case, obviously --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the Court to be free so I can direct my comments. Your Honour, the only thing that Mr. Karnavas told us just now is that it was used in another case. That still tells us nothing about the provenance of the document, where it came from. Is this a Croatian intelligence document that has purely been fabricated to put Mr. Smajkic's name on the list? We don't know where this document came from or what it is at all, and Your Honours certainly don't know and you should be told before it's put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can put it into context, first of all, with the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, when you present a document, to avoid wasting time with objections, you have to tell us where the document comes from, what the source is. It could have been produced during an examination by X or Witness Y, and it was recorded under number P whatever. So that is the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand. I understand, Mr. President, and there is a technical reason why I haven't done that. However, I do want to register my sort of discontent with the Prosecution, because he very well knows and he's merely obstructing at this point. But this particular document, as I understand it, was found within the contents of Arif Pasalic, who is dead now, and this particular document was introduced at the time in the Tuta/Stela case. And I'll be more than happy to brief the Trial Chamber at some later point on this issue, to lay a more thorough foundation. I just need some leeway. And in any event, given the Rules of Evidence, I'm merely at this point in time asking the gentleman if that is his name, if that is his date of birth, and I would like to connect it with the other document, which is 1D 00472.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that your correct date of birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can we show the gentleman the next document, 1D 00472, please. And for Your Honours, if -- and to save some time, if you could look at the second page of the actual text. It's a proposal. If it's not working on the e-court -- again, could we have Madam Usher -- it is. I don't see it. This is another document, 1D 00472. Okay. One is 427 and this one is 472. Excuse me, we could go a lot quicker if we could just put it on the ELMO. I don't see it on the e-court. I'm trying to save some time. I understand. I'd rather do it the old fashioned way, madam. Thank you. Let me have my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at the second page of this document -- well, look at the first page where it says "Proposal." It starts off with: "Smajkic Seid, son of Dervis," and it goes on and on, and the date of birth is 9 February, 1947. That would be you, would it not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you go to the proposal, ma'am. In the B/C/S, it would be the second page. It's called "Prijedlog." Okay. You could see from the very first line -- it seems to be your name, and on the very first line it seems to have the same date of birth, 9/2/1947; is that correct? I'm not interested in the content.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could flip to the next page - thank you, Madam Usher - and look at the very last line, the very last line, the second page. And, Your Honours, if you could do the same on that. You would see --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could we please zero on the language? It's not legible, at least from what I've seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be allowed to do my cross-examination. The gentleman is looking at it. If he cannot read it, he will say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't read it, Your Honours, and I'd like to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't see it on the screen. If they can enlarge on the screen, please, that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can give him a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the proposal, second page, the very last word, does it not say "Rusmir"? In fact, I'll read the last paragraph: "According to the fact that so far Smajkic put full readiness for consciously, organised undercover and consent executing of the certain tasks of service, and having in mind his honesty, willingness, and skill he has shown at these jobs, we recommend his registration as an associate of SDB under the pseudonym Rusmir." And then we have at the bottom, it says: "Approval from the chief of the centre of SDB, dated 6 March, 1980." That would be about the same time that you became chief mufti of Mostar. It says: "On the basis of Article 46 of the Rules of Procedure, SDB, registration of Associate Rusmir is approved." Were you able to read that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I have no further questions on this issue. Now, I just want to go very quickly through some of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. There was no question. We just spent ten minutes going through a document and he says, Can you read that? And there's no question or chance for the witness to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again I can understand Mr. Scott's willingness or his predilection to try to assist the witness. The question was, was he a member, early on, way back, and was he aware of public documents? He said no. Then I was told you got to show him the documents. I showed him the documents. I wanted to make sure that this was his correct date of birth. He acknowledged it. I move on. I made my point. He said he wasn't aware. I showed them. These are public documents. Now, we all are aware, I'll move on. Where is the dilemma other than obstruction from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are they public documents or are they some confidential intelligence report that this man has never seen before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's from a book, Your Honour. It's from a book. He has the hard copy of the book, he has the first page, and the Prosecution is well aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. But -- well, the Defence has showed you a document. It -- counsel read out the last paragraph. The Prosecution rose to object. Now, at this point, do you have any comments to make or are you saying that what is written down is false? Do you have a comment to make? Do you have any reaction when faced with this? There we have it. What can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Of course I do have a comment, and I have very many things to say in response, but of course I do not wish to burden you with a description of the situation that obtained at the time in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it is a notorious untruth that I was a collaborator of the secret service of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the secret security service of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is, however, true, Your Honours, that not only I myself but many religious dignitaries had occasion to have individual conversations on specific topics, and we were invited for such conversations in order to give our perception of things, of developments. In view of the fact that the former communist regime actually was against religious work, the assertion of religion as such, we were constantly under observation, so that in some situations, in some delicate situations, security staff would invite me too personally for talks. But never, ever, and I underscore that for the -- for a hundred times, I was never ever asked to be a collaborator of that service but only to impart some information which was of relevance at the time in respect of the then current interests of the service. So our trips to other countries, particularly Arabic countries - I studied in Islamic countries on a specific mission - always were attended by a network of observers, namely surveillors as to whom I had met, what conversations I had had, and so on. And as to what they put down in their notebooks and what records they had made, I really have no idea because no one ever showed that to me nor did I have any idea that such a document existed until this book was published that was today shown and which is now already accessible to the broad public. The Islamic community undertook an investigation in that respect and actually put an end to that matter as such, having come to this conclusion which I have just described. So that after such talks that we had from time to time, I have no idea what those people put down and how they portrayed those talks. Of course, they would perhaps be expected to boast that they had managed to recruit some people for their activities, but I don't know that and I can't say that was so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Counsel Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... first you denied knowing it, then you said it was published in a book, then you said that you first learned of it here, then you said that the Islamic community did an investigation. That's -- that's your answer today, in a nutshell, and that you never worked maybe other than having some informative talks with them.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we can move on. In your -- in your -- and I'm going to go through some topics, and hopefully I can be through with my cross-examination within the next 45 minutes or so. Now, when you testified last time that you were here - and this is 24 May, 2006 - you were asked a question about having to go up to Split with Mr. Topic, appearing on television, and at which time Mr. Topic had indicated words to the effect that the east side is for the Serbs, the west side is for the -- for the Croats, and of course the joke was that the Neretva was for the Muslims. Do you recall that exchange? And that could be found, actually -- I'm paraphrasing but the entire exchange is from page 2493 all the way to 2496 of the transcript dated 24 May, 2006. But you recall that exchange; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, what you -- you then went on to indicate that that more or less, at least in your mind, verified what had come out in the press that Mr. Mate Boban and Karadzic at Graz had formed an agreement?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can feel that in the field. Namely, this agreement was reflected in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get to that. We're going to get to that. But before we get to feelings and reflections, I want to make sure that your testimony was that based on Topic's remarks - and this was prior to the liberation, as I understand it, of the east side, okay? - it was your understanding and belief that Topic's remarks verified, at least in your mind, that there had been agreement between Mate Boban and Karadzic, and that's what you testified to under oath; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And in fact, a document was shown that at least does not bear the signature of Mr. Mate Boban, remember? There was -- there was an exhibit or a document that was shown purporting what the agreement was all about, but we haven't seen an actual agreement with the signature, correct, and a stamp?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall not enter into that. I did not have it myself, but there was a discussion on it last time as you yourself just indicated. There was a discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I just want to share with you -- I just want to share with you and perhaps with everyone who is following this trial a letter that was sent by Mate Boban to -- it's a public statement, actually, to the group of Croatia -- Croatians in the diaspora. It's dated 17 May, 1992, it's 1D 00428. We may need to get this on the ELMO because the signature line and the stamp may not be reflected in the e-court. Thank you very much, Madam Usher, I appreciate the assistance. And, Your Honours, I believe you might have it as well, assuming we are efficient today. And if we could look at at least the very second paragraph. Look at both pages, if you would. If you want to look at -- just look at the first page, look at the last page. I want you to look at the last page primarily so you could at least tell us whether that purports to be -- I know you may or may not be aware of the signature, but with the seal and in Boban's -- Mate Boban's signature, would -- would that at least seem to be correct? You don't know.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But nonetheless it does say Mate Boban, does it not? And that seal does look like the seal of the -- that was being used at the time by Mr. Boban; correct? Yeah, okay?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the very first page, the very first page, because we'll see there at the very top of the page on the -- on the left side, we'll see a date 17 May, 1992. 17 May, 1992. I'm underscoring that because this date, as I understand it, precedes, precedes the liberation of the east side of Mostar, which by this point was more or less under siege and occupied by the JNA, Montenegrin, Chetnik, you name it, whatever you want to call it, forces that were attacking at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the date on which activities were being undertaken to liberate the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now -- and it would seem that this date more or less coincides with your trip -- at least, if we -- if we do -- you know, if we try to factor in when you -- you claim you went to Split, this would have been just about the time that you went to Split and appeared on television with Mr. Topic, on or about. I don't know the exact date, but it's around this period. And it definitely would be post Graz meeting between Boban and Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with precision what particular date it was and whether it was after the 21st of May or on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was in the spirit. But let me just tell you, if we wish to clear things up, when Mr. Topic appeared on the screen to speak, the caption underneath --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- said the mayor --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of Mostar. So it's quite possible it was the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question was is this about the time? Yes or no or I don't know; one of the three.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you claim that based on the conversations, whenever they may be, they're in the record from your previous testimony, that Topic's remarks verified in your mind that there had been agreement between Mate Boban and Karadzic. And now what I want to do is focus your attention to paragraph 2 of this document dated 17 May, 1992. And just the very first line. I'm not going to go through the entire document. We don't have three days, as I would like to take you through to cross-examine you, but all we can see from the first line from the second paragraph: "The talks in Graz, when it concerns the Croatian side, didn't have any intention of signing any document that would contribute the splitting of BiH, or to denying rights to Muslims, the constitutive nation of BiH." It doesn't get any clearer than that, does it? You see that, do you not, sir? And by the way, he's addressing a group of Croatians in the diaspora, many, of course, have -- many of them have their own claims of where the borders of the Republic of Croatia ought to be. And yet here he is, the president of HZ HB, telling the folks out in the diaspora, who by the way - and correct me if I'm wrong - at this period in history are sending money into Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Croatians in order to fend off the Serb aggression; correct? And he's telling them this -- there was no agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's not my practice to interrupt cross-examination so often. I understand the latitude of cross-examination. But as long as Mr. Karnavas continues doing it incorrectly, I have no choice but to continue to rise to my feet. Look at your screen right now, Your Honour. I invite the Court's attention to the screen. Look at this question. Look at this question: It goes on for some 20, 25 lines of text, argument after argument after argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Don't just move on. Don't just put the question and then say "I'll move on." Either put a question to the witness or don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll do it in baby steps, Your Honour. At this point in time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, first of all, try and speak slower, please, because the interpreters are having a hard time following, and so is the court reporter, and sometimes some of your words are left out because of that. So try and do that for the benefit of one and all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm trying to work within this new system, Your Honour, of trying to condense my cross. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point in time the war was raging, was it not, in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Croats -- the Croats, like the Muslims, you know, are depending on the folks in the diaspora to send them aid, including money, to assist in their defence; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I don't think it's a great secret, we're not going to be revealing anything, that there were elements of the Croatian diaspora who had certain ideas, and perhaps even still have certain ideas today, as to how far the borders of Croatia extend to, and some may even say all the way up to the Drina. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so at this point in time, in history, when Boban, as the president of the HZ HB, is relying on financial assistance from the diaspora, the very same folks who may harbour ideas as to where the borders may be, he is saying concretely in his letter here, in his answer, that, one, there was no agreement to split up. That's what we read. Would you agree with me on that, that that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps that is what it says, but that is not a document to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- believed. It is of a duplicitous nature, as far as documents are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then it goes on that talks were held on the request of conference on BiH of the European Union and after the conference they were held bilaterally. Does it not say that? Just give me a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually did not follow this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Further down, it says: "There was no secret arrangements of splitting the BiH or 'betrayal' of anyone's interests." Do you see that? Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if we -- then if we go to the third paragraph - and this is just the last point I want to raise on this before we move on - it says in the second sentence of the third paragraph: "Representatives of Muslim people didn't show up because they couldn't leave Sarajevo due to blockades." Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm slightly lost in this text --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but if you say so. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Third paragraph. The paragraph -- third paragraph, and it starts with the second sentence: "Representatives of Muslim people didn't show up because they couldn't leave Sarajevo due to blockades." Right? And --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- historically speaking, historically speaking - just so we can thread this needle - at that particular point in time, at that particular point in time, Sarajevo was indeed under siege, was it not? There were blockades. It was being heavily attacked by the aggressors. Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on. And we're going to have to move on a little quicker than I -- hopefully I'll be a little more efficient. Now, you testified -- you -- you testified about a letter that was shown to you with respect to -- a letter that you got from Mr. Topic where you thought it was threatening in some -- in some manner. Apparently you had made some requests, and he came back, and you took that letter to be somewhat threatening. It is P 00731. If we can have it on -- on the -- on the e-court. If not, we have plenty of copies over here. I just want to touch on this a little bit and then go on to another document. But in essence - and you're familiar with this document - in this particular document he's telling you that -- that you need to devote yourself primarily to spiritual matters and not politics; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that may not necessarily be a threat, is it? I mean, sometimes politics and religion shouldn't mix. I'm not saying always, but sometimes, at least.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I felt it on my own skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, one of the complaints is about -- one of the complaints is about -- that you're raising is about the premises, that you don't have sufficient premises, you being the mufti, the head of the Islamic community, and of course you have certain responsibilities and what have you. So is it not a fact that Mr. Topic is telling you, basically, be patient? Is he not saying that? And I can read the relevant portions of it. But he's telling you to be patient. Is he not saying that? Yes or no, and then we'll move on. Okay?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the content, I don't have to read the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he says -- at least at one point, he says: "The war government of the Croatian Defence Council is working to find accommodation for your mufti offices. As soon as legally valid acts are adopted in relation to denationalisation, we shall enable the owners to take possession of their property whenever possible." He says that, does he not? Is that a yes? You have to -- for the record you have to say yes, or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the letter says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when he's talking about denationalisation, he's talking about property that was actually taken, confiscated, used, whatever the word you may want, borrowed, by the old communists or socialists, whatever your predilection is. Basically some call themselves communists, some socialists, but by and large they confiscated properties and now the denationalisation refers to giving back the property to the rightful owners; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it the Islamic community wasn't spared, like any of the other communities or individuals. Properties were taken from the Islamic community by the old socialists or communists.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the property -- actually, the communist regime took most of the property from the Islamic community at that time, as well as from other religious communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we can look at 1D 00436. 1D 00436. I don't know if it's on this electronic -- but we have the ELMO, thank God. If we can look at this document, sir, and just look at it for a second, and while you're looking at it, let me say it looks at the bottom of it, it says Friday, 24 July, 1992. It looks like it comes from a -- the Official Gazette, and it's titled "Decision on the housing of the mufti's office of Herzegovina and the board of the Islamic regional community." Does it not say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not signed by Mr. Topic. Anyone could have written this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me. It says at the bottom "Official Gazette." It's from the Official Gazette. You know as well as I do that they don't sign every decision on the actual Official Gazette. They merely publish so folks like us, later on, can see what exactly is going on in the community and what laws are being passed, and what decisions. And this in fact, sir, is not a decision, and does it not say -- does it not say that article 1: "The public housing and utilities office shall find an appropriate solution to help the Islamic religious community house the mufti's office of Herzegovina and the board of the Islamic religious community." It says that, right? It either says it or it doesn't. Does it say it? Okay, we will --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... get there step-by-step, trust me.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Then we --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are overlapping again, for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then we go to article 2. It says the business premises next to the -- this particular mosque in Racina [phoen], the former Merkur Mostar shoe shop are here by returned - returned - to the Islamic religious community since it is their rightful owner. So here is an example of a decision giving back, and so on and so forth. Now I don't want to dwell too much on this, but at least on 24 July, 1992, there is a decision published in the Islamic -- in the Official Gazette where they're attempting, at least, to return some property to -- that belonged to the Islamic community and at the same time making a promise - because that's what it says, it's a promise - shall find, okay? Does it make that promise? Yes or no. There's a promise in there.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that a solution shall be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, I don't want to -- I know that we're going -- we're not going to agree on this, whether a solution to your satisfaction was found, but you would agree with me on this, that -- hold on. I'm saying that a solution to your satisfaction was not found, was not found. A solution to your satisfaction may not have been found. However - and this is a big "however" - that period of time was a rather difficult period of time for Mostar, both west and east, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And let's face it, that city was not ready to absorb all the refugees that had come into the city and accommodate all the displaced people, including you being one of them, and all of your offices; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were problems with finding adequate accommodation and housing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would appear, at least, if I understand you correctly, we have a decision here which shows a good faith effort is being made but nonetheless you feel -- you felt then and perhaps you feel today that they weren't moving fast enough or good enough to accommodate you where perhaps, when it came to the Catholics and the Catholic bishop, they showed a greater preference or a greater expediency in trying to resolve the bishop's problems. That's what this misunderstanding was all about.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right, and that is what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- think still today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... end of the day we're going to have more in common than you think. Now, I want to talk a little bit about -- you indicated that the streets were changed, okay? Now -- and at one point a document was shown to you, and I believe it was from a Croatian -- go ahead. Keep it short. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to intervene at this point, with your permission. I went to see Mr. Topic. I went to his office and asked him to find accommodation. Please believe me. He said, "We'll find something. I'll try and find something." However, then the bishop came to see me, the new bishop, from the Vatican, coming to Mostar. I'm not sleeping nights, I can't sleep at night because I have to find him suitable accommodation. I don't mind. I like the bishop to have the right accommodation. But the building that they chose was wrong, because it was the building of the Bosniak mayor, which in a way, the person responsible should not give the residence of a mayor to a bishop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If I -- okay. I understand that you have some disagreements with respect to how Mr. Topic handled the situation, but you would agree with me, sir, that you were not the only one that was in his office, asking for premises. I'm sure there were a lot of other people, and I'm sure a lot of them feel the same way, looking at other neighbours or other friends or other individuals, thinking that perhaps they should have a better accommodation. So by and large, Mr. Topic was trying to make the best. Perhaps he could have done better for you, but at the end of the day, there's no threat in that letter. Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could go on to another issue, and that's the issue of the streets. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry. Okay. Everybody can take a deep breath, okay, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the streets. You were shown a document by the Prosecutor. I believe it was P 08538. I don't need to see it. I don't need to see it. We don't need to see it. It was from a newspaper, Dalmacija something; right? Free Dalmacija?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Slobodna Dalmacija, Free Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I may be wrong but I believe the date may have been outside of the relevant period we're talking about. It might be back 1995. But in any event, based on that document you read and you told us that certain street names were changed and certain street names were adopted that brought back memories of a very dark period. Basically the Ustasha period. Okay? For some it was a dark period, and in fact it was a dark period; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now that we agree on that, I just want to show you a decision, and this is -- I'm going to be referring to -- to 439. I guess it's D -- D -- 1D 00439. If we could look at this, and perhaps if you could have handy 440 and 462. 439, 440, 462. We'll do it real quickly. And I believe I also need to show you -- So if we look at this on 439, he says "Priority --" It's a decision. "Priority. The names of the streets in Mostar in ideological meanings will be changed." And then it goes on, Article II, all the names with Yugoslavian and ideological meanings. Again we're talking about the communists and the socialists; right? Will expire. That's what it says. That's that first decision, 439. Would you agree with me on that? Dated 6 November, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you look at another decision - and I'm looking at document 440 - on the appointment of the commission for the change of names on the streets in Mostar. Again: 440, dated 6 November, 1992. It appears that there's a department of communal housing affairs and reconstruction is in charge to recommend members of the commission for change of the names in the streets of Mostar. So it appears that a commission is going to be set up on 6 November, 1992. Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could go to 462, and here I want to draw your attention. Here's where I want to draw your attention because this appears to be the actual decision where the names are changed. We have what existed or what was being changed to. The document on the second page shows that it's 30 December, 1992. And if we go all the way down the list, we can see very clearly what is being changed, and at least my understanding from consulting with my colleagues, not having the benefit of knowing the history or the language, it would appear to me that none of these names reflect names of a dark period or names of individuals that were of a particular political persuasion, primarily fascists. Now, if we go all the way down to the bottom, the very last line - and here, Your Honours, I'm drawing your close scrutiny and attention - not only to last line but also we're going to look at your own testimony, because apparently you make reference to this particular street, and it's on page 2565 of the record dated 25 May, 2006, and in fact it's between lines 11 and 21, you, sir, mistakenly, perhaps because you were relying on a document that the Prosecution showed you, that newspaper said that the street of Aleksa Santica was changed to a Dr. Mile Budak Street.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the name stands today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't say whether it stands or not, but this is what you said. In this decision reflected on 30 December, 1992 -- now, whether it was changed later on or not, I don't know, but at least in this decision, does it not say that this very same street, Aleksa Santica is nullified and the street will be given back the previous name? In other words, they're adopting the names of the pre-socialist communist era of Racina, or Rachina, or Rasina. I don't see the accent there. Or Ricina.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ricina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: R-i-c-i-n-a. This is the very same street, is it not? At least, in this decision. I haven't been to Mostar lately to look up the street, but in this decision does it not say that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ricina is the name of an area. I live there, and within that particular area or district there is a street which is called Aleksa Santic Street which is now called Dr. Mile Budak, and now there are political battles in Mostar and there is a commission that has been set up to do away with that new name, but they haven't succeeded yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, there's a commission all over Bosnia in almost every city. You know it and I know it. But let's face it, at least in this decision, we have Mr. Topic, as of 30th December, 1992, issuing a decision that's published in the Official Gazette that the name of the street is supposed to have its previous name, does it not? Now, whether somebody else changed it later on, I don't know. I'm just showing you the decision and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a good thing had it stayed that way, or had anything been done, for that matter, along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but you acknowledge -- I guess I need to nail this point down. You acknowledge that we have a decision in the Official Gazette that is dated December 30, 1992, that does not adopt a name of some fascist doctor but, rather, it adopts the old name. That is in the Official Gazette. That's what we read. We agree on that; yes or no. Yes or no, do we agree?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just seen that. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay. Now, we're going to go to the -- now we're going to go to the names of the schools.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to refer to a document 1D 00438 - 1D 00438 - and again I have a decision here, hopefully we'll get it for you. Do we have an extra copy for Madam Usher? I think we should adopt a decision in this courtroom to just use the ELMO, Mr. President. It's much easier for me. Now, this is a decision. Again, Mr. Topic, again it looks like -- it's an official document, or it comes from the opstina Mostar. That's the municipality of Mostar; right? In here you have the preamble, and again if we look under Article 2 and you see the names that are being changed, they're changed to rather innocuous names, first primary school, second primary, third, fourth, "i tako dalje"; and so on and so forth. Right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it would appear that a lot of these things that were going on were not motivated against the Muslims, in other words that they were trying to take out a Muslim name and insert a Croat name, but rather during that period, at least, these folks wanted to get rid of any traces on streets or public buildings that reminded them of communists or socialists; right? At least that's what we see from here. Because First Primary is pretty innocuous. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And it's a public document, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Good. And incidentally, since I'm on the subject, since I'm on the subject, you indicated on the record that the name of the university was changed to Croatian University. That's in the transcript. I can get my hands on it right now, but that's what you said. And before we get to the -- before I show you these other documents, first that university had the name of a particular individual. It was a Muslim name, did it not? This institution.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in -- but that person was also a communist, was he not? First and foremost. I mean, we can agree whether -- I mean, whether he was a Muslim, a Serb, or a Croat, the bottom line is he was a communist; right? Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I guess some folks identified him with being a communist, did they not? And that's why the name was removed. And in fact, sir, in fact - because I want to speed up a little bit - you are incorrect, are you not, when you stated that the name of the university was changed to Croatian University. That is not accurate, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll slow down. Sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, it's not only a question of the university which bears the name of Dzemal Bijedic, but the post office, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mufti --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called the Croatian post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But it is your testimony -- it is your testimony -- and let me say it one more time: It is your testimony, back then and it is today, that that university changed from Dzemal Bijedic to Croatian University. That is your testimony, and I have it right here. I have you on the record. Is that your testimony? Yes, no, I misspoke; those are the three choices.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The university became the Croatian University whereas it was the Dzemal Bijedic University.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'll take that. I'll take that. Now, let's look at a couple of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be precise, Dzemal Bijedic, the name that the university took, who was this man? Who was Dzemal Bijedic? Who was he? Was he a communist? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Dzemal Bijedic was from Mostar. He was Mostar born and bred, and he was the Prime Minister of Yugoslavia. He had two terms of office when President Tito [Realtime transcript read in error "Izetbegovic"] was the president of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There you go. I rest my case. He was a communist. Now, we go on. I want to show you a couple of documents just very quickly. Document 1D 00382 and then 383. 382, 383, very quickly. I'm almost coming to the conclusion of my cross-examination. If we could look at these two documents, sir, at the very top. And I should -- and while you're looking at them, the record should reflect President Tito. This is page 39, line 9. As far as I know, Mr. Izetbegovic was never president of Yugoslavia, though he probably would have wished to have been. Okay, now, if we look at these two decisions sir, at the very top, at the very top, at the preambular, it says: Pursuant to Article 9, paragraph 3, indent 5, of degree on establishment and work of university in Mostar. University in Mostar. And it has the national gazette number 6/92, that being probably June of 1992. So here, in June of 1992, there appears to be a decision or decree -- okay. Hold on. Is this -- is this -- let me put down. If you could put down -- put the section that -- that can be seen in this open section. Okay? So you could see -- and over here, in fact, there's an appointment and the appointment is of Dr. Mehmed Behmen. Do you see that, sir? Shall be appointed the dean, the dean of mechanical engineering in Mostar. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So from this document here, at least we can glean that the name of the university is not Croatian University but, rather, it's University of Mostar, University in Mostar, to be precise, making reference to a decree that's in the national gazette. And again, because you made reference to all the Muslims have been thrown out of their positions, here we have Dr. Mehmed Behmen to be appointed a mechanical engineer, and it would be fair to say, sir, that this gentleman is a Muslim, today a Bosniak; correct? And that calls for a yes or no. Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the man. I know Mr. Behmen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, but is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there's no dilemma, there's no dilemma that it says here University in Mostar. At least, in this document. There's no dilemma.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we get the document 383, the next document. You can give these explanations to the Prosecutor because all I'm trying to establish is, based on these documents, official documents, what they reflect. These are the documents that the public would have seen, and again 1D 00383, same preambular, again University of Mostar. Date of this one is November 23, 1992. A Dr. Faruk Pavlovic shall be appointed Vice Chancellor - Vice Chancellor - of the University in Mostar. Again, Dr. Faruk Pavlovic, is he not, sir, a Muslim? And I'm sure you know the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are cadres who at that time were -- showed obedience to Croatian policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But yes, it's true that he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say this. Please allow me to finish. Just one more sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, he's either a Muslim or he's not a Muslim. He's either --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he was, yes, but I'd like to say something with respect to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that this is the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It didn't the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that. There's no dilemma on that either, and thank you for that clarification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the People's Gazette of the Croatian Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... unfortunate. It would have been nice to have a few days. Now, I want to go through the schools, because, again, there was some indication, at least from you, that the appointments in the schools had changed. And if I could go through these documents very quickly. They're 1D -- 1D 00501, 500 and 499. We can go in this order. Just very quickly. Now, just to save time, it says at the top of this document Official Gazette of HVO Municipality of Mostar, okay?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Super. Now, if we could go to this, it says the appointment of the executive principal 6 elementary school, and then we see the name Samija Sefo, and it's 8 April, 1993. Okay. The name of the school is the executive -- well, it's -- there's a temporary -- appointment of temporary executive principal of the 6th elementary school in Mostar. If we go to the next one, 1D 00500, again from the Official Gazette, again April 8. Here is the 7th elementary school appointment of the executive principal, Rasim Jakirovic. I hope I'm not butchering their names too much, but ...

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, again, a Muslim, is he not, as was Samija. They're both Muslims.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time there were only Muslims in those schools because that's -- that's right, yes, yes, but the Croatian children were not -- yes, but that's the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But -- and this is signed by --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you link the two, both parts of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. But at least -- at least they're not appointing a Croat to a Muslim school where there are Muslim children. And let's face it, there are some neighbourhoods where all Muslims, or Bosniaks, are living, and all Croats and what have you, right? So if you go up to the mahala, whatever it is, you might find all Muslim children and at least there they are sensitive enough to appoint someone of their own background as principal of that school. Okay, and you would agree if we look at the last document, 1D 00499, again 8 April, Edin Music. And this is for an appointment of temporary executive principal in the school of -- you're going to have to help me out here, sir. Dreznica, right? Again, Edin Music.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Edin Music.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Edin Music is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Super. Okay, we have one more, and this is 466. I don't know if Madam Usher has it. I have it here. We could put it on very quickly. Again, this is 24 March -- 24 March, 1993, again from the Official Gazette of the municipality of Mostar HVO, and this is for appointing of the deputy head of service of the public relations in the office of the president of the HVO. Here we have a Mehmed Vejlagic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mehmed Vejzagic. And that man changed his religion and remained a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he wasn't chosen just by chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But they're Muslims.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "he was," is that with a capital M or small M? If you recall the old days when they made the distinction between Muslim with a capital M and muslim with a small M. And for those of us who don't know, what is that distinction from the old days? One deals with religion and the other deals with nationality; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I lived at -- in those old days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And we could have some long discussions on that one, but we won't. So this one now is 448, 1D 00448. It's a decision dated 23 November, 1992, on the appointment of temporary director of Hamo Cerkic company in Mostar, and we have in -- Alija Curic.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Curic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. No dilemma there. And -- and by the way, this company, Hamo Cerkic, what does it do? It's a Muslim name, too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, well, a sewing company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, but nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Textiles. It was in the eastern part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
