utterances.text: But nonetheless, you would agree with me that she is a Muslim and she is being appointed as the temporary director of a company, albeit on the east side -- on the east side; correct? He, sorry. I don't know why I assumed it was a female. Okay. All right. Now, we --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- some of those appointments, and I just wanted to clear up a couple of matters, if necessary. This one letter, I guess I'm troubled a little bit, I have to tell you. I'm a little troubled with this P 00477. The document that was shown to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Karnavas, unfortunately, it's time to break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We were a little bit late starting, so if I could have three minutes and I'm finished. I'm finished, I promise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, but three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Three Greek minutes, which are a little bit longer than ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: P 0477, as I understand it, was a document that -- that was -- that you were shown dated 14 September, 1992. This is a document that appeared to be a copy or something that was -- yeah. It appears to be a copy. It says here "prepis," and it didn't have a signature and that was a Dr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hadziosmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get there. Now, when -- oh, "prepis," by the way, because if we look at -- if we look at the version in B/C/S, "prepis," what does that mean? Does that copy or does it mean rewrite? Okay. I'll show it to you. I'll show it to you. Sorry. Just look at it.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Prepis," as far as I understand it, this was somebody that typed out a document in the original, and that's why it says "prepis." And now you would have to go to the administrative department in town to have a stamp put on it so as to show that that copy is true to the original. So it's a form of copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and you could not have described it better. In other words --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certified copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words it's not necessarily a copy, it's a rewrite. We don't have in this document a stamp or signature, but it is your understanding, sir -- it is your understanding that this was a document that was provided to you - to you physically - by the gentleman whose name is at the end, Dr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic. Yeah, Hadziosmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Your Honour. I object to the form of the question, Your Honour. The witness did not say it is a rewrite, he said it is a copy, and only Mr. Karnavas continues to use the word it's a rewrite. The witness never said that. He said it's a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is a rewrite or is it a copy? Which of the two? A copy means it was put on a copy machine and it was copied. Or was it retyped as in rewritten or -- which of the two? To me it doesn't really matter, but which of the two? And what does "prepis" mean actually?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what is your answer to this question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is it a copy or is it a rewrite? Perhaps -- let me solve the dilemma. What does --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to -- well, I told you what it meant. It's a copy when you put it in a machine and you get a copy out. This is transcribed. You type out a document as it is, as it stands, and later on it has to be certified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's a certified copy or certified transcription, certified by someone with a stamp. But I didn't receive this from Ismet Hadziosmanovic. You might have misunderstood. We have this document, but I did not get this document from Ismet Hadziosmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So if you've understood it that way, then you've misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I understood it the way it came out in the transcript. It may be perhaps you misspoke or maybe we just misunderstood each other, but just so there's no dilemma, I did see this in the transcript itself where you said that it was provided to you, and in fact I have it here on page 2519 to -- page 2519, on 24 May, 2006, line 4: "Witness: I believe that's correct. This is what I received from Ismet without a signature whereas he sent it to various other addressees, letters with the signature." You said that, did you not? Yes or no. Maybe you misspoke but you said that because I'm sure our good translators would not have made such an error. This is what you said. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't doubt the interpreters, but I got it not -- I got it from the SDA service, not from Ismet himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's it. And let me tell you that I took part in the discussion. There's a point there when we wanted to incorporate something into the last paragraph, and Ismet put that in. And on the basis of that I can also say that the document is quite correct, because we asked Ismet as a political representative to enable us to attend funerals, and that has been incorporated into the document. So that tells me that it comes from the office of Mr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic. So somebody brought it to me from his office unsigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I think we have the complete answer on that. Okay. And with that answer, sir, I want to thank you very, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. And again, I appreciate your candour and your willingness to be cross-examined. And I hope I didn't offend your feelings in any way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, it is now 10 to 11. For technical reasons we have to contact Mr. Murphy to put matters right so we're going to take 30 minutes and reconvene at 11.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume. Can we deal with the exhibit numbers, please. Yes, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to apologise on behalf of Mr. Karnavas. He had to leave, but I'll request that the following documents be tendered: 1D 00505, 1D 00472, 1D 00427, 1D 00428, 1D 00436, 1D 00439, 1D 00440, 1D 00462, 1D 00438, 1D 00382, 1D 00383, 1D 00501, 1D 00500, 1D 00499, 1D 00466, 1D 00 -- and 1D 00488. I'd like to correct an exhibit number that was tendered yesterday. 1D 00498 is the number. That exhibit number should be 1D 00506. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard 506 and I see that it says 5.000 -- I can see now the correct number. Mr. Registrar, could we first deal with the correction of the document 506, and then let's deal with the other documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. So as requested, the previously admitted exhibit 1D 00498 is now registered as being 1D 00516 -- 506, I'm sorry. The following exhibits are therefore tendered and admitted with today's date: 1D 00505, 1D 00472, 1D 00427, 1D 00428, 1D 00436, 1D 00439, 1D 00440, 1D 00462, 1D 00438, 1D 00382, 1D 00383, 1D 00501, 1D 00500, 1D 00499, 1D 00466, 1D 00488. And this completes the list, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The last exhibit should be 1D 00448.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, it's 448.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 8. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what about 505? I think Mr. Karnavas said he also wanted to introduce that. This is the booklet on the -- I have not seen it right now, but maybe I have made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's fine. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I found it. I found it. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll continue. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mufti Smajkic, my name is Vesna Alaburic, I'm a lawyer from Zagreb and I'm representing Mr. Petkovic. I first want to put some questions to you to clarify certain subjects that have to do with the Muslim or Bosniak people. So let's talk about this for five minutes, if we may. Can you inform the Chamber and us as to when the Muslims were recognised as a people in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the first constitutional amendments introduced in 1971, was this also verified in the constitution?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1974 that was probably the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me with regard to the 1974 constitution in the former Yugoslavia -- can we find in that constitution Muslims with a capital M and muslims with a small M? Muslims with a capital M represent a people, whereas muslims with a small M represents people of the Islam religion.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As of that time, Muslims with a capital M, that is to say the Muslim people, what we call the Bosniaks today, can such Muslims be atheists, Christians, Buddhists or members of any other faith?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims with a capital M can be whatever they want to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's right, and tell me, as of that time, muslims with a small M, could such a muslim be a Muslim with a capital M but also someone who is a Croat or an American, a Brazilian, or a member of any other nation?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's possible. Would you agree with me that the term "Bosnian" is in fact a term that is common to Muslims with a capital M, that is to say to Bosniaks, and to Serbs, Croats, and members of all other ethnic groups or those who haven't declared that they are members of another ethnic group but who live in the territory of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it's therefore logical to say that Croats in Bosnia were against identifying the term "Bosnia" and "Bosnian" with the term "Muslim" or "Bosniak"?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. If -- if these terms were identified, they were said to be identical, yes, you'd be right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you mentioned the Muslims in your public announcements and your texts and so on, are you referring to Muslims with a capital M or a small M?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we should be consistent in the use of terminology since misunderstandings could arise. We're referring to the religion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You're referring to their faith, to believers.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Especially now, since 1993, the Bosniak nationality has been recognised.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that we were clear about the terms we were using when it came to discussing other subjects. In your testimony, which directly concerns my client, and in relation to Prosecution Exhibit P 02587 -- could we have this on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: P 02586, interpreter's correction. This is your request to Mr. Petkovic and Topic dated the 31st of May, 1993, and in that request you wanted peace in order to celebrate Bajram. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it before me but I'm familiar with the contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The witness can remember the document, so it's not necessary to have it on the screen, but here we have it, so we can continue. That's not the document. I have a different document P 022586 -- P 02586, but since the witness knows what document is in question, we can continue. With regard to that request, you said that the cease-fire wasn't allowed, and your testimony as recorded in the transcript dated the 24th of May, on page 134, line 19. With regard to that testimony, could we show the witness the document 4D 00016. We also have a copy of that document for our usher, who is very busy today. Yes, we'll have the digital version on the screen in a minute. Sir, could we have a look at this document. Could you tell us what the contents of this document are, who issued the document, when, and who was it forwarded to? Well, let's simplify this. Would you agree that the request to Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Topic was sent by you on the 31st of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said that on that same day General Milivoj Petkovic issued an order requesting that the cease-fire be respected? And you can see that document before you now. Would you agree with me that that's what this document that you have before you is about?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive a document of any kind, and there was no cease-fire. This is the first time I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. It's quite clear that you didn't receive the document, and it doesn't even say that it was forwarded to you here. Would you agree with me if I said that the person to whom this document was addressed can be seen in the upper right part of the document, where it says "To the commander," and then we have the abbreviation OZ JIH, which means the operative zone of south-east Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't identify or recognise anything here in the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's not in the stamp. It's not the stamp I'm talking about. You know how these letters look. In the right-hand corner you can see the person who issued the document, and then on the left you have certain identifying marks, then you have the date, the contents of the document, and then to the right you can see the person that the document is forwarded to.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says "To the commander of the operative zone." Let's have a look at the contents of the document, and would you agree that under number 1 my client issued an order to all HVO units according to which they should fully respect the cease-fire during the Kurban Bajram Muslim holiday from the 1st of June to the 4th of June, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 2 does it say that commanders at all levels have the obligation of forwarding this order to their units?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that under item 3 it says that the commander of the operative zone shall contact the commander of the commander of the 1st Corps, inform him of the order issue -- issued and request that his units also contribute to full peace? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says under item 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the lower part of the document -- and could we scroll down, please, in order to see the lower part of the document. And would you agree with me if I said that you can now see on the screen that it says that on the same day the commander of the operative zone of south-east Herzegovina, Milenko Lasic, forwarded this order to his units so that they could implement the order? Is that what the document says?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that no cease-fire was implemented after all. So could the usher please place the following document on the ELMO: The second page of document 4D 00015. This document is not available in digital form because we don't yet have the translation of the transcript from the session of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The session concerned is the 233rd. It was held on the 29th of December, 1993, and at that session there were discussions of a truce, of a cease-fire, among other things, and there's a very significant statement made by General Stjepan Siber too. Sir, General Stjepan Siber, is this a name you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this person is.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is a general of the ABiH, of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did he have a command function, a command role in the ABiH in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, but could we have the second page of that document placed on the ELMO. 84 is the number. We're interested in the lower part of the page of the session of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina in December, 1993. Mr. Kljujic, when discussing how to implement peace and put an end to the offensives said, "The only solution, Mr. Izetbegovic, is for us to stop the offensive by the 18th until there are new negotiations," and Stjepan Siber then answered: "Let me comment on the situation, with your permission. First of all, there are objections when cease-fires are signed, et cetera. We issue orders to our units. However, the orders are forwarded to the battalions, companies, and almost to each and every soldier, but believe me -" I'm waiting for the translation - "but believe me, the battlefield is so wide that you can always find someone who opens fire. I won't say on the other side, but on our side too. You always come across someone, or there is always someone who opens fire. In many places such as Mostar, you have a man every 30 metres, and there is always someone." Sir, would you agree with me if I said that in order to implement the decision, the agreement on having a cease-fire it's necessary for both parties to demonstrate goodwill? And if the conflict continues, it's not possible to accuse only one side.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to inform our Chamber of some of your statements and to comment on those statements. There was some controversial reactions to the statements you made in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I would like to refer to these statements. Could we have the following document on the screen: 4D 00029. Yes, we have it now. This is a text from the index site, and it says in the title "Anti-Semitic and anti-Christian message." So the title of the text is as follows. You can see this in the fourth line of the document. It says: "Mostar -- the Mostar mufti issued anti-Semitic and anti-Christian messages." And then it reads as follows: "In the course of a mass for the Muslim Bajram, there was a speech and there was a transcript relayed by the Herzegovina newspapers, and in that speech the Mostar mufti seriously accused -- made serious accusations against the Jews for what was happening in Jerusalem." And then it says: "Man, have a look at Jerusalem now. What's happening in Jerusalem now? Because there are Jews there, and because Muslims are not managing things, are not in power. For 100 years, during the Crusades, Christians were in power and people were up to their knees in blood -- were in blood up to their knees. It's only possible for there to be peace there once Muslims are in power, because other people are incapable of governing. They don't know the right measure, and they are unable to act in a tolerant and cultural manner." Sir, is this a statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a free interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But basically it's correct.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll comment on this. You can comment on this later on. We'll see other comments.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not avoiding this, I'd just like to say that this was called anti-Semitic, et cetera, yes, but this was an arbitrary qualification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What's important is that your words have been conveyed correctly.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the whole, yes. The essence has been conveyed correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And then the text reads as follows: You asked for a similar state in Mostar. You said that the town and the Neretva would only be appropriate for everyone if the Muslims were in power. And then allow me to read what you said. You said: "We have been the hosts in this town for 450 years. Everyone lived comfortably. Restructuring things, what does this mean? It means that -- it means that of these fine hosts who gave everyone a lot of liberty and who allowed everyone to express him or herself how he wanted, it means that we should allow someone who was setting fire to buildings the other day should have domination." Mr. Smajkic, is this what you said?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although there are certain nuances here, but yes, that's the essence of what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And there's another statement that you made. Let's see if it's been faithfully conveyed. It has to do with you objecting to the construction of Catholic religious buildings, and you said, and I quote: "Can you see that accusatory cross up on the Hum hill? Shall we go back to 1991? Take that from over there, but who will do that? They're already preparing to construct a huge church." Is this correct? Is this what you said?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not a hundred per cent, but the essence is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know how your statements were received by the public and in general in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Are you aware of the fact that the statements that you gave were used as examples of speech full of hatred in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not full of hatred.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, what such speech is like is a matter we could discuss at length. But could we show the document 4D 00032 to the witness. This is something drafted by Mr. Dusan Babic. It's called "The Language of Hate." A phenomenological and typological demonstration of speech characteristic. In this territory, it was published in the Regional Bulletin for the Promotion of Culture and Minority Rights and Inter-ethnic Tolerance. It was published on the 15th of August, 2004. Let's show the witness page 6 the last paragraph, and on page 7 the first paragraph. While we're waiting for the text to appear, I'll read for you a part of it, and you will be able to follow. The text is as follows: "Paradoxically as it may sound, the religious leaders are politically more exposed than the politicians are themselves, this being the result of the close conjunction between politics and religion. I need not even stress how deleterious this is to any modern state, community, especially if it is a multinational and multi-confessional one as the BH is." Next page, please. The text goes on to read: "The Mostar mufti Efendi Smajkic will remain remembered by his recent xenophobic statement to the effect that only the Muslims were capable of ruling the city on the Neretva, just as the Osmanlije managed to successfully rule Jerusalem for centuries. Such a statement is profoundly anti-Bosnian, because it is a real gift in the lap of and argument given into the hands of the extremists from the ranks of the two other peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina." Tell us, Mr. Smajkic, did you -- had you read this text? Did you know about it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about this text, but I denied it in both Croatian papers and different other papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What sort of a denial?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To -- of some statements regarding my statements, in respect of my statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But you did say that these statements were -- faithfully reflected your statements otherwise, so I can conclude that this retraction that you had published referred to some other statements and not these.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Exactly these. There were several papers in Croatia that sent me a query concerning these statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, let us just clarify. When I asked you about the quotation of your statement in re of Jerusalem, you said that it was faithful, and the same thing also regarding your statement in Mostar. So if these statements are basically correct and truthful, then by the logic of things, you -- there was nothing to deny or retract.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was, and how.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But obviously one usually seeks to retract things that are considered to be untrue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have two types of questions and then you are asking for an interpretation. You firstly asked whether he recognises the statements that he made, and that is in document -- the first document, number 29. He said that, yes, he made such statements. He didn't deny that. And then you showed him a document, and you mentioned two sentences in the document. It's document 32 that you referred to, and you asked him whether that is what he stated. He said no. He denied that, because what you showed to him were things that had been written by journalists. He didn't write that. And you then said, well, this is what it says. So it's necessary to make a distinction. It's necessary to make a distinction between what he said and what others said about him. So ask him to make this distinction, because otherwise it will be impossible for everyone else to follow things. I'm following things, but those who are listening to us might not be able to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My view among us who heard these -- this conversation in B/C/S, there is no misunderstanding. I cannot say anything about the interpretation into French, because I can't speak or understand French, and I wasn't able to control the translation into English well, but basically what we talked about was in regard of document 29, when I was quoting the quotations of the alleged statements of the mufti, the question was whether these were his statements that had been basically faithfully conveyed, and the response he gave in regard to all the three quotations under document 29 was given in the affirmative. Let me just explain so that -- these were not the statements of this author but conveyed statements. I just wanted us to clarify that the journalist had conveyed them correctly and that basically these were indeed the mufti's statements. And now we come to our topic. I should like to ask how this disclaimer of yours can refer to statements that the witness himself said were his and basically had been conveyed faithfully as his statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I give you an answer to that? You said a while ago that if we wanted a joint life, co-existence, that both sides to the conflict had to see to it that there should be no violation of the truce as far as the war is concerned; and as regards interpersonal relations, also of course they had to promote them on both sides. So I gave the example of co-existence in Jerusalem, and that is true. And I still assert that while the Muslims were in charge of Jerusalem as a multi-confessional place, sacrosanct place of the Jews, the Christians, and the Muslims, everybody had free access and could freely practice their religious convictions there, and that is what I stated and that is true. During the Crusades that was not possible and I said so. So to make a long story short, today when both the Christians and the Muslims are denied the right to get into Jerusalem and to do what is enjoined upon them to do by their respective religions, they are jeopardised in that sense. So that is the essence, that is the thread of my argument. Co-existence in Islam is a plank of Islam. It is a religion of co-existence and peace. As regards the cross on the Hum in Mostar, that is not only my own position. This is -- it is pointless to say -- it is senseless to say that as a religious leader I am against the cross or against any place of worship, but if you erect a gigantic cross on the Mount Hum, on the hill of Hum above the city of Mostar, which is a multi-confessional and multi-religious and multi-ethnic milieu, that is actually a message by the Croatian people to say that Mostar is Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We shall come to that during our further discussion, and let us absolve this disclaimer theme in this way: Does this statement regarding the disclaimer actually refer to the reactions, the comments made in respect of your statements?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had it published in the Jutarnji List, the morning paper. I cannot recall it exactly now. I didn't know that you would be asking me this question, but several people at the desk offices of the paper actually -- actually contacted me in respect of these few pages on the internet, the intention of which was to actually portray me as an anti-Semitic, and they asked me for a response and I gave them my interpretation in that respect and was well as in respect of Mostar. If you will allow me --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No let us follow an order and we'll come to that in due time. Tell me, did you already the past few years portray yourself in public as a person -- as the sole person since the time of the Washington and Dayton Accords that actually advocated the protection of the places of worship of Bosniaks in Mostar and the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but not only me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What -- did you portray yourself as the only person who advocated these things?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I hold a position that I could -- that put me in a position to be able to react in that way more often.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But did you portray yourself as the sole person?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Possibly. When you find yourself in a position when other people are silent and certain political influential factors not saying anything, you have to --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But did you portray yourself --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the speakers please slow down and not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So did you project yourself as the only one fighting for the protection of the place of worship and the human rights of Bosniaks in Bosnia and Herzegovina in an open letter or, rather, a reaction which was published in the papers where you said -- where you reacted, rather, to the text which was called "An Open Letter to the Mostar Mufti"?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will counsel please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Will the witness please show document 4D 0030 in which you, at the beginning of the third paragraph, say, and I quote: "After the Washington and Dayton Accords, I was the only one who got up and stood up in defence and protection of places of worship and overall human rights of Bosniaks in Mostar and in Herzegovina." Now, looking at this text of your own reaction, can you confirm that this was indeed your own reaction on the dates in question?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am concealing nothing, believe you me. The Dani, the Dani paper, before this, actually published an open -- an open letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Just confirm this. Is this so or not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they criticised the Bosniaks and the mufti, and so I raised my voice against the erection of a titanic cross on the Hum.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I am not denying that you had justification to react. I'm just asking you how you portrayed yourself to the public in your reaction. If you do confirm that this was indeed your reaction, we shall then move on to a different topic, a topic which refers to the establishment of the Muslim army. Can document -- a document we've already seen in the examination-in-chief stage, the number being D 00374, can it be shown to the witness, please. And will you just look at it to jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To use this time until this is displayed on the screen, can I just say what I'm being warned of by my colleagues; that it was not published. This was a reaction of the witness which was published in the publication the magazine Dani.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, the interpreter did not get it correctly because you overlapped. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So it's P 00374. This is a resolution of the Muslims of Herzegovina, which you are quite familiar with, but let us look at the text in order to reproduce it as faithfully as possible. Can we see item V on page 2, please. Tell us, Mufti, you were actively involved in the drawing of this resolution; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Item V, paragraph 1, you, in a nutshell, call upon all able-bodied Muslims to join in the defence of the homeland. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I quote item II: "We call upon the defenders from the ranks of the Muslims to all rally under the B and H standard and for their emblem to be the coat of arms with the golden lilies." Can you tell us if in item I you speak about Muslims, i.e., citizens of a Muslim -- of the Muslim nation whom you are calling upon to join the army to fight for the homeland, to whom does this second part refer? Who are these defenders from among the ranks of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other people there were not involved. I would have to think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Think. Perhaps I can be of some assistance. It is logical to conclude that if the first paragraph refers to Muslims who are not as yet fighters and upon whom you are calling to join the B and H army, it is logical that paragraph II refers to someone who is already within an army but is not in the BH army, and you are inviting these others to step out from that other army and rally under the B and H standard. Would such a conclusion on my part be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not perhaps fully, because -- and I shall be quite frank -- this is -- this was in August, 1992, as far as I remember, but it was the preference of a certain state of facts, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Namely to have as many Muslims possible -- as possible move from the HVO into the B and H army?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the flag of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please put document 4D 00033 on the ELMO and -- on the ELMO, because we as yet do not have integral translations of these documents, still have not put them in e-court. Ms. Usher, [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] documents. Last four documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. This is an assessment of the security situation which was compiled on the 16th of April, 1993, of the -- by the security chief of the 42nd Mountain Brigade of the 4th Corps, and that head of security is Mario Huso. And I should like to draw your attention to just one part of this assessment. Does the third line from the bottom, which says that among the measures which are to be undertaken, all Muslims, members of the HVO, are to be called upon to put themselves on the side to align with their own nation? Can we then show to the witness the next document.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. The document -- the date?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 16th of April, 1993. 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I've been on my feet and I'm not trying to interrupt but only a technical correction, I believe. I was having some difficulty a few moments ago following the document, the reference to Exhibit P 00374. At least how it came across in the English transcript -- I don't know what counsel was saying in her language, unfortunately, but at least on the English transcript, was making references to Article II, and the only language that I was able to find seemed to be in Article V. I'd just like the transcript to be corrected to reflect that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colleague Scott, would you be so kind as to tell me what particular page and line are you referring to? The resolution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm referring to the resolution of the Muslims of Herzegovina, Exhibit P 00374. In Article -- you were referring -- you were quoting language a moment ago, if I understood you correctly, "We call on all Muslims fit for military service and rallying to the Muslim cause," et cetera, and unless I missed it, the only place I see that particular language was in Article V, immediately under the heading Article V. I did not see that language in Article II, which was the reference given in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to point V of the resolution of the Muslims of Herzegovina, and that was an exhibit admitted under number P 00374. 000374. And it was point V. And the witness referred to that point and we read it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, we've seen the first document, which says that among the measures that should be undertaken in the forthcoming period is to send all Muslim -- call upon all Muslims, members of the HVO, to stand on the side of their own people.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the 16th of April. Now I'd like to have a look at the next document, and the number of that document is 34, dated the 18th of April. The author is the same. Once again, it is a proposal for security measures, and it says, among other things, the following -- once again, the third bullet point from the stop: "To establish cooperation with our fighters in the HVO and indicate the seriousness of the situation to them." Now, I'd like the next document to be shown the witness, which is number 35. And it is a document dated the 18th of April, 1993. It is an order, and I'd like us to turn to the next page of that order. As I was saying, it is an order by the commander Bajro Pizovic, in which in the highlighted portion, the portion highlighted in yellow, it says that the organ for moral guidance and morale, IPD and VP, will compile a plan for informing the populace of the composition of the brigades, the population on the territory of Mostar municipality, Capljina and Stolac, and Muslim soldiers who are located in HVO units in the aforementioned municipalities. And now the final document for the time being on that topic, and that is document number 36. It is a report by the commander of the 4th Corps. Arif Pasalic is his name, and it is dated the 2nd of May, 1993. May we see the lower portion of that document. We're interested in the lower portion. Scroll down, please. It is highlighted in yellow once again. It is a report on the activities that were implemented, and I quote: "Tying up with our people in the HVO." May I have the next side of that same document, please, the next page. In the upper portion, once again highlighted in yellow, it says, and I quote: "All the people from the HVO of Capljina have the task of taking control of the village of Tasovcici and the Capljina bridge and not allow forces to come in from the direction of Metkovic." And then the other bullet point highlighted says: "To take control of the town of Stolac with our men in the HVO." Now, my next question to you, Mr. Smajkic, is this: We have now looked at four documents related to what the BH army is doing in order to tie in and link up and work in concert with the Muslims in the HVO. Now, would it be right for me to conclude that those activities were the result of the appeal from the resolution of the Muslims of Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us why not.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't for the simple reason that I asked you what the date was, and the 15th of April is the second ultimatum posed by the Croatian Defence Council to the Muslims or, rather, so that the Bosniaks and BH army should be resubordinated and that -- to the HVO, attached to the HVO, or they will be forcefully disarmed. Now, in the field incidents had already taken place, both on the 18th and 19th. Our commander was taken prisoner. I'm not perhaps the right person and competent enough to talk about this but I would like to give you this information because I was down there at that time and I know that there was very high tension there at the time, and of course we expected an attack, so these were measures to prevent what happened from happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Smajkic, you're talking about an ultimatum again of the 15th of April, you've mentioned an ultimatum of the 15th of April, 1993, once again, but you haven't provided the Prosecution, neither has the Prosecution provided us, with any document whatsoever in which we would see this ultimatum, which would contain this ultimatum. So I'm asking you now have you ever seen a document which would include something that resembles an ultimatum with the date of the 15th of April, 1993, as you have been mentioning?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume you know about the 15th of January, 1993, that ultimatum. I assume you know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 15th of January? Well, I don't know whether we agree about how to refer to the document. I know of a document of the 15th of January, but I don't know the document you mention, an ultimatum you mention of the 15th of April, 1993, so please help us out. Help the Trial Chamber out and us out.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll be happy to do so. I'll be happy to assist the Trial Chamber and you yourself. We in Mostar on the 15th of April, 1993, on the day -- or, rather, 15th of April is the day the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established. So on that day, in view of the tensions of relations, the HVO had a show of might in the eastern part of town, and exactly on the 15th of April it had a parade, a large-scale parade with tanks and mortars and vehicles carrying --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, can we concentrate on the document concerning the ultimatum. When you mention the date the 15th of April, is that the date when this alleged document was made public?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was when the expiry date was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But when was it published?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a good question. In the western part of town I had my office, and in trying to save my head, save my life, all my documents remained in the western part of town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a document of that kind?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown such a document. It was shown to me, but as I say, my entire archive was left in the western part of town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic we don't have a document of that kind in this binder and the Prosecutor would have been duty-bound to provide us with all the documents concerned with the charges made against our clients. We don't have that document. So it's very interesting to know that you can say with certainty that a document of that kind existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, I think Ms. Alaburic has misstated the situation. As the president -- as Your Honour the President has frequently reminded us, there are something like 9.000 documents in this case. I assure the Chamber as an officer of the Court that there are indeed a number of documents which reflect the existence of this ultimatum but they weren't used with this particular witness because he did not have -- he did not actually have one in his possession at the time, as he just told us a moment ago. The fact that the Prosecution has not put any one particular document out of 9.900 documents to a particular witness has no particular significance unless this particular witness has nothing to say about it. But counsel knows well, or she should know if she's reviewed the exhibit list which she's had since January, that indeed there are documents that put -- that establish this ultimatum. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps just a clarification to Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Alaburic --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but perhaps we're talking about January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I intervene, Counsel? You've raised a problem. You indicated, with respect to this 15th of April document, that it doesn't exist. That's what you suggested to the witness. So I draw the conclusion that that document does not in fact exist, whereas the Prosecutor was on his feet and said there is a document on the list. Now, as counsel, you must have known about the list and known what's on it, on the list. So you can't say that the document doesn't exist if it's on the list you've received. I don't understand your position. Perhaps you'll explain yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll be happy to do so. Thank you. My learned colleague Mr. Scott, in his last sentence when he just reacted a moment ago, he confirmed the existence of a document that can be considered to be an ultimatum dated January, 1993. Mr. Scott did not say that there was such a document dated April, 1993. He said that documents existed which refer to alleged ultimatum from 1993. I carefully looked at all the documents that we were provided with, and of course there can be oversights. I wouldn't go so far as to say that something did not exist if we hadn't given our all to determine whether it did or didn't, and I can say with certainty that there is no document that can be called an ultimatum and which relates to the 15th of April, 1993. Now, in view of the fact that the witness has just told us that he has seen such a document, I simply wanted to clarify with him whether he had actually seen the document. Perhaps he had heard about it or seen newspaper articles and what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're dealing with the 15th of April. I was in the western section, I was in the office there until the 8th of May, which means 23 more days, 23 days after that. So if it exists, it's not up to me to find it, to find the document. The documents I had I handed over, those that were in my briefcase.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It wasn't my intention to accuse you of anything. I just wanted to know whether perhaps the document existed even if we didn't have it. But my time is drawing to a close, and I would like to ask you just one more question linked to the resolution when you yourself said that you called upon people to stand under the banner or the emblem of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you describe to us what the coat of arms of Bosnia-Herzegovina looked like at that time in the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Bosnia-Herzegovina was an internationally recognised state.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. What did its coat of arms look like?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had the lily.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And is that the coat of arms of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina today or just one entity in that state?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a coat of arms of the state itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You mean the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the flag's different, but the coat of arms basically remained the same with just some slight modifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Bosnia-Herzegovina state or are you speaking about the lily emblem in the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the federation, the entity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us whether the lily exists in the entity and in the coat of arms of the entity of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that there is a chequerboard -- as the chequerboard stands as the coat of arms of the Croats?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, Ms. Alaburic, the exhibits. Would you like to tender them?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do apologise, Your Honour. Just one moment, if I may. In the meantime, I seem to have mixed up my papers here. Ah, here it is. I'd like to have the following exhibits admitted into evidence: 4D 00016, 4D 00029, 4D 00030, 4D 00031, and 4D 00032. I would also like the following to be marked for identification before they are tendered later on: 4D 00015, 4D 00033, 4D 00034, 4D 00035, and 4D 00036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Smajkic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The following exhibits are therefore tendered and admitted as full-fledged exhibits: 4D 0016, 4D 00029. I repeat for the record the first one: 4D 00016, yes. 4D 00029, 4D 00030, 4D 00031, 4D 00032. The following five exhibits are marked for identification with today's date as tendering date: 4D 00015, 4D 00033, 4D 00034, 4D 00035, 4D 00036. These are marked for identification pending translation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's perfect. Now, on the basis of my mathematics, we have had four counsel conducting the cross-examination. We have Mr. Jonjic left and Mr. Ibrisimovic. Now, as far as time is concerned, I'd like to know how long each one of you intend to take. Counsel Jonjic, how much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have consulted my colleague Mr. Ibrisimovic, and I think that by the end of this session - and we have 15 to 20 minutes more of this session, of this sitting; is that right? - we'd be finished during the next session. But I have to add that I also spoke to Mr. Coric, and he might require several minutes for a few questions to Mr. Smajkic. We're not quite certain whether he'll wish to do so at this point. Would you like me to continue now or are we going to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So there are two possibilities. We're either going to continue straight away. In that case, that will be around 1.00. Now, I'm sure Mr. Scott will have additional questions to ask. Yes, he will certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Maybe 15 minutes, 20 minutes at the most. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think the best course to take would be to take a break now because it's 12.30. This will give a chance for us to have a rest and reconvene at 2.00 p.m., and we'll manage to finish ahead of time, I think, anyway, but anyway the meeting is adjourned until 2.00 p.m. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.35 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jonjic, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We discussed about how to divide the remaining time among ourselves. According to Defence for Mr. Pusic, Mr. Ibrisimovic won't have any questions, but Mr. Coric and Mr. Praljak said that they would like about 15 minutes each. So I'd be grateful if the Chamber could tell me how much time I have remaining at my disposal so that I can organise myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time did you plan to use up?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as you can see from the binder that I have here, there are 30 documents that I wanted to show to the witness, 30 documents I wanted to ask the witness about. I don't know whether that will be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have 30 documents that I do not have. I apologise. They've just been provided to me. So you have 30 documents. Given your professional skills that you have demonstrated so far, I believe you can get through them very rapidly. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Smajkic. My name is Tomislav Jonjic, and I have a series of questions that I would like to put to you on behalf of Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Given your testimony over a one-and-a-half-day period when examined by the Prosecution, and you've been now cross-examined for a day -- just over a day by the Defence, I think you would agree that since September, 1991, Mostar was in fact an occupied town.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: In April, 1992, the JNA launched very open attacks, together with other forces that had joined it.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, does the name Suad Cupina mean anything to you? I'll repeat the name for the sake of the transcript. Yes, it's been correctly transcribed. Suad Cupina, does this name mean anything?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Mr. Cupina was one of the main individuals responsible for the organisation of the ABiH in Mostar and he was the first commander of the Mostar Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the position he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You undoubtedly know that recently Mr. Cupina published a book entitled "Betrayal and Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1991 to 1995."

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: You reviewed the book?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Your review was at least partially published in that book as part of that book.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of my review is included in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: You praised the book extensively. You said it was an excellent and reliable source of information for the history of the pre-war and wartime events in Mostar and its surroundings.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: And today, would you still praise that book? You have no objections to raise with regard to the contents of the book?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to go into the details, but on the whole -- well, it's the author who wrote the book, but I like the substance of the book, the essence of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the following document: 5D 01113. Could the registry find this document. It's an excerpt. I apologise. The first number was the correct one after all: 1113. It's an excerpt from Mr. Cupina's book. We should have it on the screen. Yes, there it is. Could we have a look at the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, why am I showing you this excerpt from the book? Well, because you spoke about the problems with regard to establishing the HVO. Here we have a copy of pages 460 and 461 in the book, and in the last paragraph Mr. Cupina describes how on the 5th of April, 1992, together with the SDA leadership Mr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic and Zijad Demirovic, they met Mate Boban in Grude and they also met Brano Kvesic there. And then in the last paragraph on this page it says Mr. Cupina in fact describes how they were to appoint units the purpose of which was to defend Mostar. They were supposed to designate such units. And then Boban issued an ultimatum. That's what Cupina says. Could we have a look at the following page. He said: "Let Sarajevo decide within a week whether the joint defence of Mostar will be called the Muslim-Croat Defence Council or the reverse." Is that correct, Mr. Smajkic? That's what it says in the book.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. I can read that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's correct. A few days ago, in response to questions put to you by Mr. Stojic's Defence team, you informed the Chamber of some HVO documents, and in the heading of those documents it was not possible to see the symbol of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry now show us the following document: 5D 1114. 1114. While we are waiting for the document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1104.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, in some HVO documents there were -- were no symbols of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you said that revealed the real intentions of the Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: If you have a look at this document now, you can see that the heading says the Croatian Defence Council. It says the Independent Battalion, the Independent Mostar Defence Battalion. It says strictly confidential, we have the date the 8th of May, 1992, and if we scroll down -- could we please scroll down right to the bottom of the document -- we'll see that the document has been signed by Mr. Cupina and that Mr. Pasalic is being appointed to the position of battalion commander, Mr. Arif Pasalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's correct. Could we scroll up again. Can we see the symbol of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina here?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: But this is a document signed by a unit which is considered to be the beginning of the ABiH in Mostar; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry please show us 5D 1105.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Once again we have a document from the Independent Mostar Defence Battalion. It's dated the 9th of May. Mr. Smajkic, would you agree that the heading again says the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council, and yet again we can't see the symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: And the signatory - if we can scroll down - we'll see who signed the document. The person who signed the document is Mr. Cupina once again. Isn't that correct, Mr. Smajkic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, can we draw the conclusion that Mr. Cupina and the Independent Mostar Defence Battalion deny the statehood or the existence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document shows that there was a form of joint coordination and that the Independent Battalion accepted HVO leadership in order to defend themselves and liberate themselves from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is given the fact that the symbol of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has been omitted, is it possible to draw any conclusions as to the position of the person who drafted the document with regard to the existence of that state?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't draw any conclusions from this document on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry now show us the following document: 5D 01106. So 1106 is the number of the document. So far we have seen documents signed by Mr. Suad Cupina, documents that don't bear the symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Could the registry now show us the signatory. Could we scroll down to the bottom of the document now, please. Unfortunately, this scanned digital version doesn't reveal the identity of the person who signed the document but the original does. We could place the original on the ELMO, and I'd like to do so with the assistance of the usher. We'll thus be able to see who the signatory of the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, we can see that the signatory is Mr. Arif Pasalic. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Mr. Pasalic replaced Mr. Cupina at the head of the Independent Battalion and then in the autumn of 1992 he became the commander of the 4th Corps of the ABiH; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: If we return to the digital version of this document - I assume it will be simpler to proceed in this way - then at the top of the document we'll see that the date is the 15th of May, 1992, and we'll also see that the document doesn't bear the symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Isn't that correct, Mr. Smajkic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Pasalic also signed documents the heading of which didn't contain the symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Since we're discussing this document, if we have a look at the middle of the document we'll see that it mentions the strength of the battalion. Mr. Smajkic, would we agree that this is immediately prior to the liberation of the town of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about a month prior to its liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Could we scroll a little further down, please. Can you tell us what the total strength of the Independent Battalion was? 569. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the number 569? Can you tell us, in the town of Mostar and the surroundings, how many Muslim military conscripts were there, in your assessment, and how many refugees were there from Eastern Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Last week in the course of your testimony you said that according to the documents of the Cultural Circle of Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina, there were 17.000 mainly Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the number, 17.000, but there were men from other areas and they weren't only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: But given that in your assessment, does this number 569 represent a significant military force? You have certain military skills as well, I know that.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a significant number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry please show us 5D 0107 -- 1107 and 1108. Those are the documents we'd like to see on the screen. Again, we're interested in the heading of these documents and we'd like to see whether Bosnia-Herzegovina is referred to in the documents that are of, let's say, Muslim origin or, rather, they're documents that were drafted in the Independent Defence Battalion. So the number of the document I was referring to is 1107. No. Something's not quite right. 1107. It's a document dated the 2nd of June. 1107. We have it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, yet again we have before us a document that doesn't bear the symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's dated the 2nd of June, and it's been signed by Mr. Pasalic. Mr. Pasalic contacted the Municipal Staff of the HVO in Mostar. He is asking for weapons, ammunition, et cetera, isn't that correct, and it didn't bear the symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You keep emphasising this fact. This is a compromise. It was important to liberate the town, and we believed that this issue would be solved at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Please don't try to interpret these things, just try to answer the questions since we don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we now have a look at the document number 5D 01108. 1108. Could the registry please put the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: This is a handwritten document, and again here do you agree with me, Mr. Smajkic, it doesn't bear the symbol of the B and H?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: And if you can see the Croatian version, it is signed -- or the Bosnian version, if you will. We have the English translation now on our screens. So this document was signed by, of course, if -- we'll see that if you scroll up a bit. So it is Hasan Breko, the commander of the 1st Company of the Independent Battalion, and the date is the 12th of July, 1992. Do you know Mr. Breko?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the 12th of July is almost a month after the liberation of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. Thereabouts, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Okay, yes, thank you very much. And after the liberation of Mostar, the documents of the Independent Battalion still fail to bear the symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And talking about symbols and emblems, will the registrar please show us document 5D 010 -- sorry, 5D 01109.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this document to be displayed, I shall tell you, Mr. Smajkic, that this is an order from 1992. We don't know the exact date because it is not there, issued by the military police of Travnik. And if we can see the document, then we can perhaps deal with it. Here it is. So this is the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it says the Muslim forces of Travnik; right, Mr. Smajkic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: 1992. We see the signatory and with some sort of a stamp. Tell me, is this stamp -- you discussed this -- the stamp used also with my Colleague Nozica that was used or not used. Tell me, this stamp that we see on this document, is it in any way whatsoever connected with Bosnia and Herzegovina and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: You spoke Arabic, of course. Can you translate for our benefit what the stamp says, the top part of it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Allah is the only god and Muhammed is his messenger."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will the registrar show us document 5D 0110. If it is -- if there are difficulties, we can see it on the ELMO. 5D 01110. Well, if we can't do it, perhaps we can show it on the ELMO. Well, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, as you can see on the top, the 8th of May is written by hand, and this is a list of members of the HVO Independent Defence Battalion, battalion for the defence of Mostar, who have been issued with an automatic rifle. I presume that you know some of these people on this list. Tell me, under number 9, do you see the name Zijo Demirovic, Sosi?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: He was among the leaders of the SDA in Mostar, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: So one cannot conclude on that basis that he was also a soldier. Not only was he formally a military conscript but he was indeed a soldier because he had been issued with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was not a soldier because he did not go to the positions. I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: But you see him on this list.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: And you see his nickname, Sos. So it couldn't be a person bearing the very same name and surname. I mean, this -- that distinction would be obvious, given his nickname.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Will the registrar please scroll the document up so we can see the end of the document. All the way up. Yes, thank you. Under number 25, Mr. Smajkic, we have Arif Pasalic. First the command -- deputy commander and later the -- of the -- that is of the Independent Battalion, and later the commander of the 4th Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that name is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: And can you read just the first line of this remark, of this note down here. If it is difficult for you, I will assist you. So it says, "The automatic rifles have been received from the Main Staff of the HVO." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: So we see for that this group of the members of the Independent Battalion as well among whom there also are prominent political and military officials from among the ranks of the Muslim nation, they have been issued their weapons by the HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will the registry please show us document 5D 01111. So it's four 1s in a row. And while we wait for that document, Mr. Smajkic, I will ask you to confirm for me that a couple of days ago you referred to the fact that the Muslims were systematically pushed out of posts in the social and public life, political life in Mostar. Today we saw -- in some of the exhibits presented by the Defence of Mr. Prlic some different thesis being advanced. Tell me, in 1991, 1992, and 1993, especially were Muslims indeed suppressed from such positions in social and political life?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We now again see the book of Suad Cupina that you revised [as interpreted], that you lavished praises on. Will the registrar please show us the following page. So this is a reproduction from the book of Mr. Cupina. It is a list of directors and principals of elementary and secondary schools. Mr. Smajkic, would you be so kind as to take a quick look at this list of names.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Can the registrar please scroll the document down. Can you take a look at these names as well.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Can we have next -- the next page, page 229 from the book, or the next page in this document. These are directors of cultural institutions, et cetera. I should like to kindly ask you, Mr. Smajkic, again to take a look at this list.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: Can you find the name of a single newly appointed director who is not a Muslim, a single one?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an explanation for this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for any explanations. You have seen 30 or 40 names of newly appointed directors. I'm just asking you whether a single one of them is not Muslim.
