utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You did not appoint anyone who was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't appoint anyone, nor were there any foreigners in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "that unit," which unit are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the unit in which we appointed Nemir Ibrahimovic, this Muslim forces unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction of the name: Mimic Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, a number of questions were put to you by various Defence counsel about this publication called "Instructions to the Muslim Fighter." Once again, there are a number of times when you attempted to give a broader explanation of various points made, and I simply want to give you an opportunity clarify anything that was put to you in relation to the publication "Instructions to the Muslim Fighter."

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to thank the Chamber too. I can't really say that my convictions were in some way unsettled, but I do know some people, Halil Mehtic, Hasan Mekic, and certain other individuals who were active, and if they drafted a text or a brochure, given their qualifications and their moral positions, I don't believe they could have drafted some sort of a text that would have spread hatred and animosity towards someone else. The very title "Instructions to the Muslim Fighter" demonstrates that these are suggestions that concern a moral code for Muslim fighters. They're told not to steal, to act in a disciplined way, to demonstrate solidarity, concern, et cetera, et cetera. And above all, they're strictly ordered not to kill women, the elderly, children. They mustn't destroy places of worship, et cetera. So these are general civilised standards of behaviour. In one of the sentences in the text, and responding to Mr. Praljak to an extent, in one of the sentences it's not a fight against non-Muslims. And I'm glad I've found this part. It says that the greatest jihad is to tell a leader, a despot, a man of power, that he is wrong and that he is not acting properly. You can find that sentence in that text, and you have got this document on your list as one of the documents that is to be translated. So it's not matter of encouraging people or fighters to kill. It's more a matter of avoiding unnecessary acts. If weapons can be kept silent, they should be kept silent. They should not be used. War is war, and when people are arrested, certain things happen. In all armies there are differences between releasing prisoners, exchanging prisoners, requesting ransoms, and in extreme and rare cases the court-martials that can process certain cases and mete out the death penalty. But this doesn't concern this first area I was talking about. After the instructions on behaviour, it says that these suggestions that Muslim fighters have to adhere to. However, if certain things happen, then you have to act in certain ways. When arresting individuals when they're -- acts of the slaughter are carried out, when very serious crimes are committed in the course of military operations, then there is a particular law that comes into force, that is valid, and this naturally concerns Muslim states. But we were not concerned; we didn't have such intentions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak is on his feet. Usually in the course of the re-examination there should not be any other interventions, but, Mr. Praljak, what is the problem? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Mr. Smajkic, I never commented at all on the "Instructions to the Muslim Fighters." I said on the basis of the documents shown to this Court and in this court, the Muderiz Brigade, in its structure, in its line-ups, always uttered the following words: "All of you together: Whom are you fighting for?" The response was: "For Allah." And then the next question to the brigade was: "Against whom are you fighting?" The Muderiz Brigade replied: "Against the Vlahs." So I just provided an explanation which I think was in order, that in Bosnia and Herzegovina the concept of the Vlahs encompassed Catholics and Orthodox, the Orthodox. I'm not talking in general terms. This referred to the Muderiz Brigade specifically. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You've already said that, though. Mr. Scott, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D 00428.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. As a reminder, sir, this is a letter that apparently, according to the Defence, Mr. Boban wrote on the 17th of May, 1992. Can you assist the Judges, Mufti Smajkic, by saying, to your knowledge, was this letter written by Mr. Boban, was this written after there had been an international outcry and rejection of the secret bilateral talks between Karadzic and Boban?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas this morning showed you some documents about the -- or at least a document - perhaps several - about the names -- streets, the changing of names of streets and other names in Mostar. And can you assist the Judges, please, just -- apart from what the documents said on their face, did that in fact happen? That is, were these names actually -- and street signs and names actually changed pursuant to the documents that Mr. Karnavas showed you, if you know or can recall?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, I do know. This did not happen in practice in this section, in this part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying you don't contest the documents Mr. Karnavas showed you, but in reality, there were no positive effects as a result of this change.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some changes did take place in the west part of the city, whereas in the so-called eastern part of the city the names of streets were not changed, and that is the truth. We did not want to do that, Your Honours, precisely because we were committed to preserving the unity of the city. We wanted to reach an agreement in some way. Of course, in the west part of the city there were also some names with some Muslim dignitaries, some street names bearing the names of Muslim dignitaries, not all Bolsheviks, as they say. So somebody perhaps might object to that -- those streets having such names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So based on the documents we saw this morning, we had the impression that they were Bolsheviks, but you said, no, they were not just Bolsheviks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the witness could next be shown, please, Exhibit 1D 00382. If we could see that, please. Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm just double-checking the reference. Just as an example, sir, Mr. Karnavas showed you also a series of documents about the appointments of various Muslims as schoolteachers or various other positions, and once again, Mr. Karnavas said if anyone -- anything more needed to be said, the Prosecution would give you an opportunity to address that, so I want to do so. So is there anything more you want to say about the appointments of various Muslims as schoolteachers or other positions as reflected in the documents Mr. Karnavas showed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scott. You just read my thoughts. I think that this is -- it is of decisive importance to know this. We have not come here to try and outwit one another, because in the documents you can find this and you can find that. I am a homegrown person, a person of the people, and I know. I'm familiar with these things much more than other people are. So believe me, just like in the case of the appointment of the first government in which the Muslims -- to which the Muslims and the Bosniaks were appointed, believe me in this particular instance, and I stand by this, invoking my oath: You could see that in 1991 and 1992, 19 -- and these two years, most of the principals of schools were indeed Muslims, but it is important to know that the Croats had relocated their children from Mostar as a war zone and had their children educated either in Western Herzegovina or in Croatia. So it is only logical that the authorities were -- organised things in this way later. However, there was a transformation, and I can say that these -- this Muslim personnel was removed from their positions en masse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. Mostly a point of clarification: In questioning today that had to do with the time period April, 1993, in one of your answers you said -- you made reference to -- that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established on the 15th of April. Now, can you tell the Judges whether that -- were you referring then at that moment to the celebration of the one-year anniversary or that the army was created in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you exactly what this is about. Namely, it is possible that there was a discrepancy, that there was -- there were differences as to which date to take and whom which date suited, whether it was the defence, the Territorial Defence, the Patriotic League, or the Independent Battalion, and so on. But let me repeat first and foremost: I'm not a soldier, but I was around these people as well as around politicians, because simply the times were such. This was a struggle of a people for bare survival, and it was about saving human lives. I know, because I attended the ceremony marking the day of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that was the 15th of April. So the 15th of April is the day which commemorates that date. This year we attended the ceremony as well. I wish to say that it was precisely on that date that the HVO made a show of force in the east part of the city, pulling in formidable hardware into the city, tanks and multi-barrel rocket launchers and what have you, which were hooked up to tracks, vehicles, and mortars and such. All that meant to associate people to that 15th of April date as the date the army was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but this is supposed to be a redirect examination, and what's happening here is that Mr. Scott is asking completely open-ended questions, allowing the witness to make a speech that often has no relevance whatsoever to the question, and, Your Honours, since we have very little opportunity, if any, to respond at this point, it's a completely inappropriate way to conduct a redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will agree on this particular occasion Mr. Smajkic's answer is probably a bit longer than it needed to be. Let me repeat my original question and I will indeed ask Mr. Smajkic to be as responsive as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I just simply wanted you to clarify. You said just a moment ago again that the formation of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is celebrated each year on the 15th of April, and can you just tell the Judges, what was the first year -- what was the date, the 15th of April of what year when the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was first established?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the date that was officially taken - of course, I'm no expert on the issue - but the official date of its establishment was that. Of course, there existed different units before and after that during the resistance period, but that was taken as the official date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, I'll try one more time, and if we don't get it I'll move on. All I'm asking from you is to clarify the year, because earlier today that was said in context of 1993. I want to make sure there was no confusion. In what year -- 15th of April in what year was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina established?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be quite clear, the army was created in 1992, and on the 15th of April, 1993, there was an anniversary. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now it's clear for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You did it much better than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness to be shown Exhibit 5D 01083. And this is my one of last two or three questions. Let me know when you have that, sir.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can -- if the registry can go -- move down into the -- some of the text of that document so we can just refresh ... Let me direct -- if I can direct the registry's attention, I don't know -- it's page 373 of the B/C/S version. I don't have an ERN number. It should be about the fourth or fifth page of the document. I'm sorry. Could we go to 5D -- there are multiple excerpts from the same book. Could you give me 5D 01083 -- 84, excuse me. And just in looking at that as we're looking, we'll go to another page in a moment, but are you familiar with this publication? At any time have you seen this publication prior to today?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm directing your attention to the page that's on the screen now, the reference to Mr. Muftic and an excerpt that was given concerning Mr. Muftic and at least in the English translation it refers to Mr. Muftic as a leader of a terrorist group. Now, do you have any information apart from what it says on the face of this page whether that's true information or an accurate characterisation or not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity. In response to a question from the Defence, I said that I had never seen that book before, which is what I told you, but in trials before Yugoslav courts at that time, 10 individuals from this group were shot in front of a firing squad, and this was a matter that couldn't be publicly discussed, it couldn't be openly discussed. I haven't read this, but superficially I could say that people involved in investigations obtained by force declarations from these 10 individuals who were publicly executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to cut you a little short again to avoid objections by counsel and use our time wisely. Just specifically let me ask you this in light of what you've already said: When did this execution occur? When were these men killed by firing squad as you've just indicated?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 1947 to 1949. From 1947 to 1949, that's the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, various things that Mr. Jonjic showed you in these documents after document after document, do you have any reason to believe, for example, that this document has anything to do with anything that happened in Mostar in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And final question, sir: Mr. Coric asked you some questions about the removal of democratically elected persons and specifically the removal of Mr. Hadziosmanovic from one of his positions. Can you just clarify for the Judges, please: The removal of Mr. Hadziosmanovic, was that from a political-- internal political party position or was that from a position as an elected public official?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed by the SDA party leadership. He wasn't elected at the first democratic elections. To be 100 per cent precise, I would say that Mr. Tarik Muftic, a surgeon from Mostar, was the first SDA president in Mostar. He had political ambitions. He was an elderly man. But then Mr. Hadziosmanovic took over. And naturally we didn't have the right to replace him, but we informed his superiors that what he was doing was not correct. As citizens represented by him, we thought it was our right to object to individuals who represented the certain party or the interests of the Muslims in a political sense. And since this is very important, Mr. Hadziosmanovic was president of the SDA Municipal Board and of the Regional Board. So we had objections from towns, from the region of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from Prozor, Konjic, Jablanica, Stolac, et cetera. This was not acceptable. There were these lobbies -- there was this lobbying. So they contacted the mufti, who was some figure of authority, in order to try to have him removed, at least from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mufti. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usually after re-examination there should be no more interventions unless it's for some exceptional reason. In that case, you should ask for our leave. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking for your leave to ask some questions that concern two questions put by the Prosecution, and it concerns the appointment of school principals. I have documents that relate to this. I want to refer to certain parts of the decision concerning changing the names of streets in Mostar, and this hasn't so far been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't really see why that would be important. You've shown documents -- you showed documents in the course of your cross-examination, numerous documents which everyone followed. When re-examining the witness, the Prosecution asked the witness whether the names were all Bolshevik names or whether they were Muslim names too. The witness said they were Muslim ones. So does your question cast any doubt on -- on the answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason for changing the names of the street in the decision, and they are mentioned in the decision, will cast light on his testimony. As far as appointing directors of schools in Mostar is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, please put your questions to the witness, but very rapidly.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I first go through the documents. It will be very quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could the usher show document 1D 00503. Further cross-examination by Ms. Tomanovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Smajkic, you can see a decision on appointing an acting director of the school in Blagaj. Can you read out his name.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Akif Balalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, is he?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you please read out the date of the decision.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I see the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagaj is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please, don't forget that I'm in charge of these questions. Could we see the following document: 1D 00502.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we have a problem with the e-court, I have a hard copy for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, you can see a decision on appointing an acting director of the 4th Primary School in Mostar. Can you read out the name of the person. Please read out his name.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will. Muslija Jugo. We've seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, we haven't. Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you read out the date. When was he appointed?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I see the next document, 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have two new documents here and two new names. We have the date April, 1993. What was the purpose of the exercise? Put the question to him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose is since Mr. Smajkic said that all the directors of the primary schools were replaced later on, well, we never -- he never defined when this occurred, and I want to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, put a direct question to him. I'll do it. You said that there were appointments of Muslim directors, Muslim principals, and they were replaced or dismissed later on. So when would you say that they were dismissed? You've been shown documents showing that they were appointed in April. So when would you say that these individuals were dismissed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are purely Muslim areas. Blagaj, where Akif Balalic was the director, is an area in which only Muslims live, and that is the case for the 4th Muslim -- the 4th Mostar school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We want to know whether the teachers who were appointed, the Muslim ones, remained in their positions or were they dismissed? Defence counsel wants to show that they were not dismissed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps there were re-elections. Perhaps they were there and they remained there in those positions, because those areas were Muslim areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you just tell me, with regard to this decision, who signed the decision that you have on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Topic was the president of?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we can now go back to the decision on appointing and -- on -- the document concerned is 1D 00462, and it's the document on changing the names on the streets. We can use the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not on the screen. At least, not on mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Smajkic, if you can -- if you can please just scroll this document down a bit. In fact, can the document be moved up a bit? A bit more down, so that we can see the entire paragraph number II. Mr. Smajkic, would you please read out paragraph number II, paragraph number II of this decision.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this, "The individual ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I mean that.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The individual restoration of the earlier designations, the renaming and the name of streets and processes shall be a lengthy process which the commission shall undertake on a continuous basis and for which it is eliciting the ideas -- soliciting the ideas, proposals and assistance of the citizens of Mostar and other citizens of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which may be forwarded in written form to the address of the Croatian Defence Council of Mostar municipality." Shall I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please do, the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To the commission for naming and renaming of the streets and squares in Mostar municipality. By renaming the streets and squares, we wish to return to the citizens of Mostar -- we wish to repay the citizens of Mostar for we have never accepted the names of those who -- whose sons and grandsons destroyed the city."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this decision was intended for the citizens of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for giving me this opportunity. I just have one question when I have this opportunity. Can ask you for your leave to ask a question regarding the practical application of the instructions given in the booklet "Instructions to an Islamic Fighter"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ma'am. Further cross-examination by Ms. Nozica:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Smajkic, today in reference to the first section of the book which are some -- which is actually moral guidance to the Islamic fighter, you said that the second section was intended for those who were to act so only in the case of extreme -- in the case of extreme necessity. So I'm going to ask you, do you know that during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina this provision was at all applied by ritual killings of prisoners? Do you know of any such instances? Of course the provision of this booklet.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about one or two cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this concludes your testimony. I thank you for coming to The Hague on a number of occasions, but it was necessary. I wish you a safe trip home, and I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now give Defence for Prlic -- for Mr. Prlic the floor. They want to -- or Defence counsel wants to tender some documents into evidence. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D 00502, and 1D 00504 are the two documents I wish to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Those two exhibits will be therefore be tendered and admitted with today's date and the following references: The first one is 1D 00502, and expectedly, the second one is 1D 00504. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll go back -- we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that we are in open session, the hearing is adjourned, and the next hearing will be held on the date that I've already mentioned, thank you.
